task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) review of REQ-202's design (lib/letflow/design/req202-artifact-repository.md), checking all 14 acceptance criteria, the no-implementation-code rule, the per-tenant-vs-global placement reasoning, and whether the four stated open questions (OQ-1..OQ-4) are legitimately deferrable to ELIXIR-DEV or must be resolved now.

checks_performed.no_implementation_code: PASS -- zero markdown code fences in the entire document (grep '```' returns nothing); no literal .ex/.exs bodies or SQL statements, signatures/type shapes only.
checks_performed.promotion_digest_citation: PASS -- read lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_digest.ex L87-104 directly. Confirmed: canonicalize/1's final clause (L104, `defp canonicalize(value), do: value`) passes every non-map/non-list/non-atom value through unchanged, including numbers/floats. No number normalization exists anywhere in the module. Design's §0 and §3.2 citation is accurate, not merely trusted from the requirement's paraphrase.
checks_performed.decision_0003_citation: PASS -- read 0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md in full. Decision B's stated reasoning is confirmed as a physical-isolation/blast-radius argument ('a bug that forgets a tenant_id predicate ... fails loudly ... instead of silently leaking rows'), matching the design's §1.2 quotation. Decision C (event-table immutability as application-layer, not DB-layer) is correctly characterized and correctly distinguished from this design's DB-trigger choice.
checks_performed.req195_trigger_precedent: PASS -- read req195-audit-entry-storage.md §2 directly. Confirmed: per-tenant-schema-qualified trigger function raising a fixed-text error, wired as BEFORE UPDATE (and BEFORE DELETE for audit_entries), created inside the same `if prefix() do ... end`-guarded migration block, no shared public-schema function. Design §5 copies this pattern accurately with artifact-specific message text.
checks_performed.placement_reasoning_internal_consistency: PASS -- §1's per-tenant-vs-global argument is internally consistent and does not merely restate Decision B by default; it directly engages REQ-202's own stated tension (cross-tenant dedup forfeited) and gives a reasoned basis (no AC requires cross-tenant dedup; Decision B's isolation rationale argues against a shared-row model; workload-realism argument; batch-consistency argument). Persuasive against the 14 ACs as written -- AC1 is satisfiable per-tenant and no AC anywhere requires cross-tenant sharing.
checks_performed.traceability_sample_AC3: PASS -- §3.4 rule 3 states the integer-valued-float normalization rule concretely (no decimal point, no exponent) and ties it to AC3's exact wording. AC3 only requires the integer-valued case, which is fully specified (non-integer float format is correctly out of AC3's scope, see OQ-1).
checks_performed.traceability_sample_AC7: PASS -- §5.1 specifies the DB-level BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger mechanism concretely, matching AC7's 'rejected by the DATABASE' requirement.
checks_performed.traceability_sample_AC9: PASS -- §6 specifies ordering, parent_version_id inclusion, and REQ-067 cursor-contract reuse concretely.
checks_performed.traceability_sample_AC10: FAIL -- AC10's literal text requires the per-tenant-vs-global placement and its reason to be 'stated in the migration' (i.e. in the migration file itself, machine-checkable from the migration source), distinct from AC11's separate, explicitly-different requirement that the migration-058-vs-045 conflict be recorded in 'the moduledoc.' The design's §1 gives extensive placement reasoning, but that reasoning lives only in this design document -- §2 (the Migration section) contains no instruction that the migration file must carry a comment recording the per-tenant decision and its reason. The §10 traceability table maps AC10 to '§1' without noting this file-vs-doc distinction, so as written the design does not produce a migration file satisfying AC10 literally; ELIXIR-DEV would have no design instruction to put this reasoning where AC10 requires it to be checkable.

oq_evaluation.OQ-1_non_integer_float_decimal_form: Legitimate deferral (b) -- REQ-202's own text and the design's available R-Co citations specify only the integer-valued-float case; no acceptance criterion (AC3 included) exercises the fractional-number format. Correctly left to ELIXIR-DEV with a moduledoc-documentation requirement attached. No rework needed.
oq_evaluation.OQ-3_json_content_type_set: Legitimate deferral (b) -- no AC depends on charset-parameter or +json-suffix handling; requirement text does not enumerate the set. The design already recommends the narrowest reading as a default, which is sufficient guidance. No rework needed.
oq_evaluation.OQ-4_artifact_id_semantics: Legitimate deferral (b) -- none of the 14 ACs reference artifact_id's generation/semantics; REQ-202's schema spec lists the column but is silent on its population rule. No rework needed.
oq_evaluation.OQ-2_promotiondigest_moduledoc_vs_AC5: MUST BE RESOLVED NOW (a), not deferred -- this is exactly the failure mode this session's REQ-195 CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR precedent rejected: an AC-interpretation question flagged as uncertain rather than answered. Analysis: AC5 has three clauses -- (i) canonicaliser is a separate module, (ii) promotion_digest.ex 'is NOT modified (confirmed by git diff --stat)', (iii) 'BOTH moduledocs cross-reference each other'. Clauses (ii) and (iii) are in direct tension on ANY reading: promotion_digest.ex's moduledoc currently contains no reference to Canonicaliser, so satisfying (iii) ('BOTH... cross-reference each other') requires editing promotion_digest.ex, which git diff --stat will show as touched -- there is no way to make 'both' moduledocs cross-reference each other without editing both files. The design's own option (b) ('satisfy AC5 literally by putting the full cross-reference only on the Canonicaliser side... not in promotion_digest.ex itself') does not actually satisfy AC5 either: it satisfies clause (ii) but violates clause (iii), since then only ONE moduledoc (Canonicaliser's) would reference the other, not BOTH. So (a) and (b) are not two equally-valid readings of one ambiguous AC -- (b) is demonstrably a partial failure of AC5's own explicit text, and (a) (edit both moduledocs; read 'is NOT modified' as 'no behavioral/functional modification', i.e. no change to canonicalize/1, compute_plan_digest/1, or verify_digest/2's logic or specs) is the only reading under which all three clauses can be simultaneously true. This is derivable now, from AC5's text alone, without needing R-Co source or any implementation-time information -- it is not a legitimate Step-2a judgment call, it is a requirements-interpretation the design stage owns. The design must commit to reading (a), state explicitly why (b) fails clause (iii), and instruct that the commit/PR description documents the moduledoc-only nature of the promotion_digest.ex diff so a human/CI reviewer checking 'git diff --stat shows promotion_digest.ex touched' understands this is the intended, AC5-compliant outcome rather than a violation.

issues: lib/letflow/design/req202-artifact-repository.md §9 OQ-2: remove the 'flagged... does not resolve the tension unilaterally' framing. Commit to reading (a) explicitly: promotion_digest.ex's moduledoc MUST be edited to add the reciprocal cross-reference (this is required, not optional, to satisfy AC5 clause (iii) 'BOTH moduledocs cross-reference each other'); 'that module is NOT modified' in AC5 is read as 'no change to compute_plan_digest/1, verify_digest/2, or canonicalize/1's behavior/specs' -- a moduledoc-only diff. State explicitly, as part of this resolution, why option (b) (cross-reference on the Canonicaliser side only) does NOT satisfy AC5: it would leave only one of the two moduledocs referencing the other, violating the 'BOTH' clause outright, so (b) is not a safe fallback reading -- it is a different, additional AC5 violation. Update §3.2's 'Required moduledoc cross-reference' subsection to state this as settled, and update §10's AC5 traceability row to no longer cite OQ-2 as an open item.

lib/letflow/design/req202-artifact-repository.md §2 (Migration): add an explicit instruction that the migration file itself (not only this design document) must carry a comment recording the per-tenant placement decision and its reason (the same substance as §1.2's reasoning, condensed), so that AC10's literal text -- 'the two tables' placement ... is stated in the migration with its reason' -- is satisfied by something checkable in the migration source, distinct from AC11's separate moduledoc-recording requirement. Update §10's AC10 traceability row to point at this new instruction rather than at §1 alone (§1 is design-document reasoning, not an instruction for what the migration file must contain).
